decisions.decision: Approve the four-product catalogue and 20 listing labels for fixture use
decisions.rationale: David completed human review; approval is recorded additively and does not unlock production

decisions.decision: Keep exact manufacturer models as canonical measurement inputs
decisions.rationale: Strict identity prevents variant contamination; eligible product price relatives are aggregated into the user-facing index

decisions.decision: Apply fixture review through a least-privilege additive database function
decisions.rationale: Reviewed revisions supersede rather than mutate drafts; the NOLOGIN reviewer role has no direct table-write privileges and all locks remain engaged

decisions.decision: Do not treat the 12-product catalogue as sufficient market coverage or a production basket
decisions.rationale: A single unavailable/EOL model, missing major brand such as Corsair, or unrepresentative family concentration could undermine reliability. Maintain a broad monitored universe, reviewed reserves and explicit product-churn resilience instead.

decisions.decision: Approve the DDR5 market-universe and index-resilience architecture for continued fixture-only work
decisions.rationale: The long-lived index needs broad major-brand discovery, lifecycle evidence, reserve candidates, explicit basket vintages and single-product-loss resilience. News is explanatory and can expose catalogue gaps but cannot change the numeric index.

decisions.decision: Keep manufacturer diversification as a separate checksum-pinned candidate tranche
decisions.rationale: First-party Corsair, ADATA and Patriot evidence broadens the monitored-universe pilot without rewriting reviewed fixtures or implying source, eligibility, methodology or production approval. ADATA packaging-derived kit interpretation remains an explicit human-review caveat.

decisions.decision: Approve selected Corsair and Patriot diversification products for fixture use; hold ADATA and abstain on Lexar
decisions.rationale: Corsair and Patriot have strong exact-MPN first-party kit evidence. The ADATA Dual Tray records remain research-only until literal complete-kit evidence is retained. Lexar is neither approved nor rejected because normal-access first-party evidence could not be retained without questionable crawler impersonation.

decisions.decision: Keep the public frontend primary-retail only; defer marketplace and second-hand display
decisions.rationale: David corrected the public scope on 2026-08-09. The earlier checksum-bound non-retail publication artifact remains immutable for audit but is not imported by the public application. The site exposes retail scope, qualification rules and release gates; no verified series or outbound product links are currently public.

decisions.decision: Build candidate retail movement per retailer-product line before any product-level aggregation
decisions.rationale: This produces real deterministic movement without silently choosing a cross-retailer minimum, median, daily deduplication or threshold. Multiple same-day eligible observations fail until an explicit selection rule is approved.

decisions.decision: Retain current exact-MPN primary-retail item prices as append-only private research history even when landed-price qualification abstains; keep source authority separate from factual eligibility and keep all production, methodology, index and publication gates locked.
decisions.source: David approval plus independently verified 2026-08-09 candidate tranche

decisions.decision: Start a prospective private quoted-item relative diagnostic now; do not backcast or publish it as the index
decisions.rationale: The immutable 2026-08-09 tranche is sufficient to freeze an inception basket at 100 for deterministic future comparison. Four lawful archived observations provide useful private history, but their sparse captures, separate schema and unresolved landed-price semantics do not support silent rebasing or an official index.

next_action: Collect a second prospective immutable tranche for the same three retailer+MPN lines. Replay the private diagnostic from the frozen 2026-08-09 inception, but keep it private and explicitly not-an-index while fixed-destination delivery, availability treatment, retailer/source coverage, basket construction and methodology approval remain unresolved.
context_notes: Four checksum-pinned Wayback observations plus three immutable current observations now render as seven private item-price points across three exact seller+MPN lines. A separate deterministic prospective diagnostic can start at 100 without inventing historical index values; historical backfill is excluded from that calculation by schema and later backdating fails closed.
blocked_publications: Public frontend remains primary-retail only and shows an honest collection-start state with no publishable point or active scale. Private history and the quoted-item diagnostic are not approved indices and remain excluded from the public build.
blocker_workaround_context: Continue prospective append-only collection now rather than waiting for perfect history. Archived observations may extend private context only; they cannot revise the prospective inception, resolve landed-price semantics or bypass source, methodology, basket, production or publication locks.
